newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals says misunderstanding over rand remarks.
newsitem.headline: Stals says misunderstanding over rand remarks.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday there had been an "unfortunate but forgiveable misunderstanding" over his remarks about the rand made to Reuters on Tuesday which sent the currency sharply lower.
Reuters quoted the central bank head saying that there had been "a little bit of an over-adjustment" in the currency.
Stals said in a statement on Wednesday that the quotes attributed to him in the report were "absolutely correct as far as I can recall", but that there had been a "slight misunderstanding".

"His (the Reuters reporter) question referred to two aspects, namely 'the recent sharp rise' and 'the rand's level'. My remark of an over-adjustment referred to the 'recent sharp rise' and not the 'level' of the rand," Stals said.
"The qualification added 'but what is the right level of the rand?' and the further explanation given by me should have explained it."
Stals went on to say in his comments on Tuesday that the Reserve Bank's position was that the right level of the rand was the one where the markets were comfortable with it.
The following is a transcript of Stals' comments to Reuters on Tuesday made before a media briefing in Cape Town:
Q: Given the rand's recent sharp rise, are you happy with the rand's level?
A: "I think there is a little bit of an over-adjustment but what is the right level of the rand?"

Stals then said the Reserve Bank's position in the past had been that the right level of the rand was the one where the markets were comfortable with it, adding: "We must be consistent and we say the same now."
Q: Do you think the market is comfortable with the rand's present level?
